issues.legal_issue: A writ challenge to land acquisition proceedings may be refused for laches when it is brought only after substantial delay and after the award has been made and possession taken.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the acquisition declaration more than two years after it was made.
By the time they filed that challenge, an award had been made and possession had been taken; possession had also been handed over to the public-purpose corporation.
The challenge alleged that the declaration had been made beyond the statutory time limit, but the Court did not decide that issue on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed and the High Court’s orders were set aside because the challenge was brought after gross delay. The Court did not decide whether the declaration complied with the statutory time limit.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its discretionary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, a court should be loath to quash land-acquisition proceedings when there is inordinate delay and the award has been made and possession taken; such challenges should ordinarily be brought at least before the award and taking of possession. The Court relied on Swaika Properties (P) Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan, Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Industrial Development Investment Co. (P) Ltd., State of Rajasthan v. D.R. Laxmi, Municipal Council, Ahmednagar v. Shah Hyder Beig, and C. Padma v. Deputy Secretary to the Government of Tamil Nadu.

rule.if: land_acquisition_writ_challenge and substantial_delay_after_declaration and award_before_challenge and possession_taken_before_challenge

predicates.land_acquisition_writ_challenge: A writ petition seeks to invalidate land-acquisition proceedings.
predicates.substantial_delay_after_declaration: The landowners waited a substantial period after the acquisition declaration before challenging it.
predicates.award_before_challenge: The acquisition award was made before the landowners filed their challenge.
predicates.possession_taken_before_challenge: The authorities took possession of the land before the landowners filed their challenge.

issues.definition: When a writ challenge to land-acquisition proceedings follows substantial delay and is filed after both the award and taking of possession, the challenge is rejected for laches.
